Eight-year-old Jamin wasn’t very smart. Or at least that’s what his older brother told him. Almost daily, brother Kenny found ways to remind Jamin of his shortcomings and laugh at his blunders.

“Jamin, you will never be smart”, Kenny said. Deep inside Jamin felt resigned to a life of muddled trip-ups. Would he always be clumsy? Would he always say things wrong? That’s what Kenny said.

Jamin believed Kenny’s lectures with wide-eyed belief. Kenny was three years older than him, so he must be right. Very well, then Jamin would be simple. Kenny would be smart. Life was not fair. Dad and Mom disliked Kenny’s proud talk and punished him whenever they walked in on one of his speeches. But Kenny had a way of avoiding earshot. So he continued mocking Jamin.

Grandma Otto watched these trials from her rocker on the porch. She was a quiet old lady.

“Jamin, do you know where Kenny is?” Mom asked with a smile. “It’s almost supper time.”

“He went to check his coyote traps. I’ll go find him.”

There was a chill in the air as he tramped up over the lawn, and the sun was growing old as he crossed the border of the woods. The fleeting shadows scurried over the hills. The chill deepened as he stumped further in. He breathed the rich air and followed Kenny’s trail. Eventually, the trail would end up in a meadow, but Jamin hoped he would find Kenny before he had to go that far. The various traps had been checked already, so Jamin knew Kenny had come this way. Jamin trudged on resolutely. His golden head caught the tired beams that fled from the sun as they flickered through the trees. And soon those too had faded leaving behind the musky smell of the woods. The fall webworms had been at work, and their web curtains shuttered from branches overhead.

At length, as the trees subdued and thinned, and the meadow appeared Jamin knew this was the end of his brother’s trap route. If Kenny wasn’t here, he wouldn’t know where else to look.

But Kenny was there. As Jamin clumped into the meadow, he could see a frustrated heap to his right. The heap’s voice had a familiar ring. The heap’s face was lit in pain. The heap was Kenny. “Are you alright? What happened?” Jamin felt strange, seeing Kenny scrunched in the dirt. Kenny was smart. “Did you step in a trap?”

“Yes, Jamin. I..I wasn’t looking where I was going. Help me. Please.”

Jamin bent and found an ankle firmly held in the jaws of a steel trap. Darkness stained the ground around Kenny. Quickly, Jamin’s strong arms pried open the jaws. Kenny reeled free. “Can you walk?”

“Yes. I think so. If you support me, I can hobble along.”

“Dad and Mom will be worried. We’ve missed supper.”

Sure enough, as the brothers hobbled back through the woods, they heard the long calling of their father. Jamin called back, and he was by their side in a moment, seeing the ankle and scooping up Kenny like a hurt sheep. The odd little band hurried home, and the screen door banged shut as Dad swept across the porch. Jamin went to the wash house and scrubbed his hands. He headed for the front door.

“Jamin.” It was Grandma. The porch light showed her in her old rocker. A heavy comforter lay on her shoulders.

“Yes, Grandma?”

“Do you think you are not very smart?”

“That’s what Kenny says.” Jamin squirmed.

“You were strong enough to open the trap, and Kenny wasn’t. You were brave enough to find him in the dark. Lots of young boys wouldn’t be.” Jamin was silent. Grandma Otto rocked some more, then smiled. “God made you the way you are for a reason, Jamin. He made Kenny the way he is for a reason. He has a plan for you, and a place only you can fill, you know.”

Jamin turned and walked into the warm kitchen. He was smiling.

Agtjarige Jamin was nie baie slim nie. Of althans, dit is wat sy ouer broer vir hom gesê het. Byna daagliks het broer Kenny maniere gevind om Jamin aan sy tekortkominge te herinner en te lag oor sy misstappe.

“Jamin, jy sal nooit slim wees nie,” het Kenny gesê. Dieper binne-in het Jamin onderdanig gevoel oor ’n lewe vol verwarde struikelings. Sou hy altyd onhandig wees? Sou hy altyd die verkeerde dinge sê? Dit is wat Kenny gesê het.

Jamin het Kenny se lesings met groot oë geglo. Kenny was drie jaar ouer as hy, dus moes hy reg wees. Wel, dan sal Jamin eenvoudig wees. Kenny sal slim wees. Die lewe was nie regverdig nie. Pa en Ma het nie van Kenny se trotse praat gehou nie en het hom gestraf wanneer hulle hom tydens een van sy toesprake hoor praat het. Maar Kenny het ’n manier gehad om buite gehoorafstand te bly. So het hy voortgegaan om Jamin te bespot.

Ouma Otto het hierdie beproewings van haar stoeltjie op die stoep afgekijk. Sy was ’n stil ou dame.

“Jamin, weet jy waar Kenny is?” het Ma met ’n glimlag gevra. “Dis amper aandete.”

“Hy het weggegaan om sy jakhalslotte na te gaan. Ek gaan hom soek.”

Daar was ’n koue in die lug toe hy oor die gras trap en die son het oud geword toe hy oor die grens van die woud stap. Die vinnige skaduwees het oor die heuwels gehardloop. Die koue het verdiep toe hy verder intrek. Hy het die ryk lug ingeasem en Kenny se spoor gevolg. Uiteindelik sou die spoor in ’n weiding uitloop, maar Jamin het gehoop om Kenny te vind voordat hy so ver moes gaan. Die verskeie lokvalle was reeds nagegaan, dus het Jamin geweet Kenny het hierdie pad geloop. Jamin het vasberade aangestap. Sy goue kop het die moedervlak strale gevang wat van die son gevlug het terwyl hulle deur die bome geflikker het. En binnekort het ook dié vervaag en die muskuskruid van die woud oorgebly. Die herfspinnekopwebbe was aan die werk en hul webgordyne het van takke bo afgeskuif.

Uiteindelik, toe die bome tot bedaring kom en dunner raak en die weiding verskyn, het Jamin geweet dit was die einde van sy broer se lokvalroete. As Kenny nie hier was nie, sou hy nie weet waar anders om te soek nie.

Maar Kenny was daar. Toe Jamin die weiding instap, kon hy regs ’n gefrustreerde hoop sien. Die hoop se stem het ’n bekende klank gehad. Die hoop se gesig was van pyn verlig. Die hoop was Kenny. “Gaan dit goed met jou? Wat het gebeur?” Jamin het vreemd gevoel om Kenny in die grond opgekroes te sien. Kenny was slim. “Het jy in ’n lokval getrap?”

“Ja, Jamin. Ek… ek het nie gesien waarheen ek loop nie. Help my. Asseblief.”

Jamin het voorgebuig en ’n enkel gevind wat ferm in die kake van ’n staallokval vasgehou is. Donkerheid het die grond om Kenny besoedel. Vinnig het Jamin se sterk arms die kake oopgebreek. Kenny het vrygekom en gedraai. “Kan jy stap?”

“Ja. Ek dink so. As jy my ondersteun, kan ek strompel.”

“Pa en Ma sal bekommerd wees. Ons het aandete gemis.”

Reg so, toe die broers deur die woud terugstap, het hulle hul pa se lang geroep gehoor. Jamin het teruggeroep en hy was gou by hulle, het die enkel gesien en Kenny soos ’n seer skaap opgetel. Die vreemde klein groepie het haastig huis toe gehaas, en die skermdeur het toegeslaan toe Pa oor die stoep ingeloop het. Jamin het na die waskamer gegaan en sy hande geskrop. Hy het na die voordeur gestap.

“Jamin.” Dit was Ouma. Die stoeplig het haar in haar ou stoeltjie vertoon. ’n Sware kombers het oor haar skouers gelê.

“Ja, Ouma?”

“Dink jy jy is nie baie slim nie?”

“Dis wat Kenny sê.” Jamin het ongemaklik geskrik.

“Jy was sterk genoeg om die lokval oop te maak, en Kenny was dit nie. Jy was dapper genoeg om hom in die donker te vind. Baie jong seuns sou nie.” Jamin was stil. Ouma Otto het verder gewieg en toe geglimlag. “God het jou die manier waarop jy is om ’n rede gemaak, Jamin. Hy het Kenny die manier gemaak waarop hy is om ’n rede. Hy het ’n plan vir jou, en ’n plek wat net jy kan vul, jy weet.”

Jamin het omgedraai en die warm kombuis binnegestap. Hy het geglimlag.

Our Father’s world is a world unspoiled by human invention and intervention. While sin and technology have warped and stolen many lovely things from the human race, there abide still a few that remain unmarred by civilization. Little children in the fresh innocence of their unsoiled morning top the ranks as a bit of heaven on earth and call all observers heavenward. Another is the fowl of the air as prescribed in Genesis. Paul pleaded with the Corinthian church, “Doth not nature itself teach you?” We are exhorted to consider the lilies, the ravens, and the grass of the field. Each of these bears a significant dimension of the eternal God in their existence and gives us definition to their Creator. Perhaps all of nature can give us snapshots into heavenly places if we had the time and eyes to observe it.

Birds hold a unique place in God’s creation, for their sphere is in the heavens. Man may mount on the wings of a plane and evade the lower earth for a few hours, but the heavens will never be a place of his common dominion. The birds are a picture of a heavenly race, for they are at home there. They are a natural representation of the saints and angels of God and so we do well to give them due attention. While there may be dozens of lessons to be drawn from these vessels of grace and beauty, one of the most prominent and outstanding virtues will be observed in the song that they raise. Many animals dwelling on the earth are virtually mute. Of the ones that do speak, it is often to threaten or express complaint. “Doth the wild ass bray when he hath grass? Or loweth the ox over his fodder?” (Job 6:5). When they are happy and content, they have no message to convey. The dog barks at an intruder to drive him away, while the cat mews for attention. They speak when they are threatened or dissatisfied, in fear or in pain. Similarly, the earthly human shares its nature with the mammals of the field.

Birds are diverse. They exercise their joyous vocals so much that they are the epitome of happiness. The expression “happy as a lark” is so common a term that it is used by people who have never even ventured to the meadow to see or hear a lark. While some may inform us that these songs are mere mating calls and have little to do with their feelings, we cannot escape the inner conviction that, whether mating or not, these birds delight in bearing a jubilant expression of joy and we do well to let them teach us. “Is any merry? Let him sing psalms” (James 5:13). The birds do this incessantly and it seems impossible to draw any other conclusion but that they are happy while doing so. Wander near the nest of a swallow and you will find that they have ways of expressing depreciation as well. The killdeer also has no qualms with expressing rash disfavor to those who intrude their domain, but these are not to be mistaken as songs. The singing birds are a beautiful painted picture of the saints and angels of God.

How little knowledge of heaven is committed to our understanding. The scenes of heavens described and laid out before us in Revelations can hardly bring our finite minds into its infinite realm. One dimension that we can connect with is that it is a place filled with singing. Little wonder, for it is the culminating end of the contented and joy-filled saints of God, and there they will sing a new song. Nearly every scene at the throne in Revelations is marked by some dimension of praise. “And he hath put a new song in my mouth, even praise unto our God” (Ps 40:3). On 22 occasions, the Scriptures reiterate the phrase, I will sing.

It is the nature of the birds to sing. It is their waking thought as morning guilds the sky, and it flows from within them like a fountain. Not all of their songs are alike. Some are elaborate in their duration, meter, and pitch, while others are plain. Some merely chirp with a merry heart. The robin opens up the choir in early spring, but his song is soon surpassed in beauty by the song sparrow and again by the rose-breasted grosbeak. The song of the wren trumps them all for longevity and vibrancy. The canary sings in a cage, while the nightingale sings in the dark. The robins sing in the rain. The buntings fill in the heat of the day when other birds are silent. As diverse as their song may be, they all commonly burst forth in exuberant happiness. It is here that they shall instruct us.

“Speaking to yourselves in psalms and hymns and spiritual songs, singing and making melody in your heart to the Lord” (Eph 5:19). The advent of Christ was marked by the angelic host announcing peace and goodwill toward men. All those who will bear His name must deliver the same tidings. In John 4, we happen upon the scene at Jacob’s well, where Christ asks the woman for a drink. Her reply seems to bear a tinge of bitterness. “Jews have no dealings with the Samaritans.” Though she esteemed herself as a spiritual person and willingly followed Him into religious discourse, she had no song. Like the well that they speak over, her water was buried deep below the surface and how laborious the effort to bring it forth. Christ offers another alternative. “But the water that I shall give him shall be in him a well of water springing up into everlasting life” (John 4:14).

The well of Christ is an artesian well. One needs neither pitcher nor labor to draw it out, for it spews forth abundantly on its own accord. While Christ is probably speaking of the Spirit as in John 7:38, surely this may be just as applicable to a joy-laden heart. What is a more apt outpouring to flow from a Christ-inspired wellspring than the rapture of a song? “Behold, my servants shall sing for joy of heart” (Is 65:14). Now this should all seem plain enough to understand and easy enough to do but, alas, we find we have a constant and persistent adversary who seeks to thwart our song. We are not unaware of his devices...

Sin. Not all birds sing. There are some whose visage is black as sin. These only seem to screech and scream and are no example for the saints of God to emulate. The babbling noise we hear emanating from many passing vehicles certainly parallels the songs of such foul fowl. “Babylon the great is fallen, is fallen, and is become the habitation of devils, and the hold of every foul spirit, and a cage of every unclean and hateful bird” (Rev 18:2). These abundant creatures are the fallen spirits, the fowls waiting to devour the seed sown by the wayside. Of such are the worthless blackbirds, starlings, and grackles. The crows show themselves also at the roadside, feeding on rotting carcasses. Often you will find them in large numbers feeding themselves on the corn the farmer painstakingly planted for himself. So transgresses the selfish soul in his pursuit of happiness, feeding gleefully on the calamity of another and exploiting their sin. He bears no song, for his day is constantly clouded by the misdeeds of others who cross his path.

Neglect. The cowbird is also black (the female is brown/gray). She will be found sitting on a high vantage, shamelessly calling to her lovers by her shrill screeching. She then has the audacity to lay her egg in another bird’s nest, forcing them to raise her offspring. This is certainly a fitting emblem for a good number of females in our day. Though justified by circumstances, these women care not for their own, but are products of neglect. They have no lullaby to share with their young, for they have escorted them to the nest of another while her mind is preoccupied with work and business. “But thou art he that took me out of the womb: thou didst make me hope when I was upon my mother’s breasts” (Ps 22:9). No doubt that the singing mother can implant copious songs in her infant and set the stage for a happy and hope-filled life. While we may show mercy to a woman in dire circumstances, the major song of modern women bears chords that are but dissident and melancholy. These are stopped-up wells like unto the wells that Isaac found upon his return to Gerar. The Philistines “had filled them with earth” (Gen 26:15). So run the spiritually neglected homes of many families today, who pack their schedules so full of earthly commitments that they have no time to spend an hour in song together. If the birds stopped singing, would they even notice?

Ingratitude. Find a soul bathed in unthankfulness, and you will find a soul without a song. If the canary were to refuse to sing in captivity, few of us would ever have heard his rollicking melody. “We hanged our harps upon the willows in the midst thereof. For there they that carried us away captive required of us a song; and they that wasted us required of us mirth, saying, Sing us one of the songs of Zion. How shall we sing the LORD’S song in a strange land?” (Ps 137:2-4). God’s people had been instructed by Jeremiah to build houses, plant gardens, and raise families. “… And seek the peace of the city whither I have caused you to be carried away captives, and pray unto the LORD for it: for in the peace thereof shall ye have peace” (Jer. 29:5-7). But they could see no worth in it. With their eyes fixed upon the dismal scene around them, they lost their song. Israel had within its history a rich tradition of song. Their singing erupted at the passage of the Red Sea in the days of Jehoshaphat and had been known to defeat armies. Earthly discomfort is no excuse to withhold gratitude, for our God reigns, and we are His children. Such were the conditions of the Philippian prison where two jailbirds, Paul and Silas, opened the concert at midnight and rocked the corridors with their joyful singing.

When we open our mouths and stretch our vocals in praise, we enact the grace of God. We join the faithful choir alongside Miriam, Deborah, and Hannah, and blend harmoniously with Moses, David, Paul, and Barnabas. At evening, we sing with our Lord and His disciples after supper, and with legions of angels “giving glory to God in the highest.” If that isn’t enough, perhaps we should consider rising at early dawn and singing with the innumerable hosts of our feathered friends who are thankful for God’s loving providence. “Let the word of Christ dwell in you richly in all wisdom; teaching and admonishing one another in psalms and hymns and spiritual songs, singing with grace in your hearts to the Lord … And whatsoever ye do, do it heartily, as to the Lord, and not unto men” (Col 3:16, 23).

Ons Vader se wêreld is 'n wêreld onbesoedel deur menslike uitvinding en inmenging. Al het sonde en tegnologie baie lieflike dinge van die mensdom verwring en gesteel, bly daar steeds 'n paar wat ongerep deur beskawing voortbestaan. Klein kinders in die vars onskuld van hul onbesoedelde oggend staan bo-aan die rangorde as 'n stukkie hemel op aarde en roep alle kykers na bo. Nog 'n is die gevleuelde wese van die lug soos voorgeskryf in Genesis. Paulus het met die Korintiërs gesmeek, “Doth not nature itself teach you?” Ons word aangespoor om na die lelies, die rawe en die gras van die veld te kyk. Elk van hierdie dra 'n betekenisvolle aspek van die ewige God in hul bestaan en gee ons 'n beskrywing van hul Skepper. Miskien kan al die natuur ons beeldjies van hemelse plekke gee as ons net die tyd en oë gehad het om dit te beskou.

Voëls hou 'n unieke plek in God se skepping, want hul sfeer is in die hemel. Die mens mag op die vlerke van 'n vliegtuig klim en die laer aarde vir 'n paar ure ontwyk, maar die hemel sal nooit 'n plek van sy gewone heerskappy wees nie. Die voëls is 'n beeld van 'n hemelse ras, want hulle voel daar tuis. Hulle is 'n natuurlike voorstelling van die heiliges en engele van God en daarom doen ons goed om hulle behoorlik aandag te gee. Al mag daar dosyne lesse uit hierdie vaartuie van genade en skoonheid getrek word, een van die mees prominente en uitstaande deugde sal in die lied gesien word wat hulle ophef. Baie diere wat op die aarde woon, is byna stom. Van diegene wat wel praat, is dit dikwels om te dreig of klagte uit te spreek. “Doth the wild ass bray when he hath grass? Or loweth the ox over his fodder?” (Job 6:5). Wanneer hulle gelukkig en tevrede is, het hulle geen boodskap om oor te dra nie. Die hond blaf vir 'n indringer om hom weg te jaag, terwyl die kat miaau vir aandag. Hulle praat wanneer hulle bedreig of ontevrede is, in vrees of in pyn. Net so deel die aardse mens sy natuur met die soogdiere van die veld.

Voëls is uiteenlopend. Hulle oefen hul vreugdevolle vokale so gereeld uit dat hulle die toonbeeld van geluk is. Die uitdrukking “happy as a lark” is so algemeen dat dit gebruik word deur mense wat nog nooit eens die weide betree het om 'n lewerik te sien of te hoor nie. Al mag sommige ons inlig dat hierdie liedjies bloot paringsroep is en min met hul gevoelens te make het, kan ons nie ontsnap aan die innerlike oortuiging dat, of hulle nou paring het of nie, hierdie voëls verheug is om 'n jubelende uitdrukking van blydskap te dra en ons doen goed om hulle dit te laat leer. “Is any merry? Let him sing psalms” (James 5:13). Die voëls doen dit onophoudelik en dit lyk onmoontlik om tot enige ander gevolgtrekking te kom as dat hulle gelukkig is terwyl hulle so doen. Wandel naby die nes van 'n swaeltjie en jy sal vind dat hulle ook maniere het om misbilliging uit te druk. Die killdeer het ook geen huiwering om onbesonne afkeer te toon teenoor diegene wat hul domein binne dring nie, maar dit moet nie met liedere verwar word nie. Die singende voëls is 'n pragtige geskilderde beeld van die heiliges en engele van God.

Hoe min kennis van die hemel is aan ons begrip geopenbaar. Die tonele van die hemele wat in Revelations beskryf en voor ons uitgelê word, bring skaars ons eindige gedagtes in sy oneindige ryk. Een aspek waarmee ons kan verbind, is dat dit 'n plek vol gesang is. Geen wonder nie, want dit is die kulminerende einde van die tevrede en vreugdevolle heiliges van God, en daar sal hulle 'n nuwe lied sing. Byna elke toneel by die troon in Revelations is gemerk deur 'n aspek van lof. “And he hath put a new song in my mouth, even praise unto our God” (Ps 40:3). Op 22 geleenthede herhaal die Skrif die frase, I will sing.

Dit is die aard van die voëls om te sing. Dit is hul wakende gedagte as die oggend die hemel vergul, en dit vloei uit hulle soos 'n fontein. Nie al hul liedere is dieselfde nie. Sommige is ingewikkeld in hul duur, maat en toonhoogte, terwyl ander eenvoudig is. Sommige tjirp bloot met 'n vrolike hart. Die rooibekkant sluit die koor in vroeë lente oop, maar sy lied word gou in skoonheid oortref deur die song sparrow en weer deur die rose-breasted grosbeak. Die lied van die wren oorheers hulle almal vir volharding en lewendigheid. Die kanarie sing in 'n hok, terwyl die nagingale in die donker sing. Die robyns sing in die reën. Die buntings vul die hitte van die dag toe ander voëls stil is. So uiteenlopend as hul lied ook mag wees, barst hulle almal gemeenlik in uitbundige blydskap uit. Hier sal hulle ons onderrig.

“Speaking to yourselves in psalms and hymns and spiritual songs, singing and making melody in your heart to the Lord” (Eph 5:19). Die koms van Christus is aangemeld deur die engelaarmee wat vrede en welwillendheid teenoor mense aankondig het. Almal wat sy naam sal dra, moet dieselfde boodskappe bring. In John 4 kom ons by die toneel by Jakob se put, waar Christus die vrou vir 'n drinkvra. Haar antwoord blyk 'n spoor bitterheid te hê. “Jews have no dealings with the Samaritans.” Al het sy haarself as 'n geestelike persoon beskou en bereidwillig gevolg om in godsdienstige gesprek te tree, het sy geen lied nie. Soos die put waaroor hulle praat, was haar water diep onder die oppervlak begrawe en hoe moeisaam die poging om dit na vore te bring. Christus bied 'n ander alternatief aan. “But the water that I shall give him shall be in him a well of water springing up into everlasting life” (John 4:14).

Die put van Christus is 'n artesiese put. Mens het geen kruik of arbeid nodig om dit uit te trek nie, want dit spuit op sy eie oorvloedig uit. Al praat Christus waarskynlik van die Gees soos in John 7:38, is dit sekerlik net so toepaslik op 'n vreugdegevoede hart. Wat is 'n meer toepaslike uitstrooming om uit 'n Christus-geïnspireerde fontein te vloei as die vervoering van 'n lied? “Behold, my servants shall sing for joy of heart” (Is 65:14). Nou behoort dit alles eenvoudig genoeg te wees om te verstaan en maklik genoeg om te doen, maar, ach, ons vind dat ons 'n konstante en volgehoue teenstander het wat ons lied wil verhoed. Ons is nie onbewus van sy wapens nie...

Sonde. Nie alle voëls sing nie. Daar is 'n paar wie se voorkomen swart is soos sonde. Hierdie lyk net te kraai en te skreeu en is geen voorbeeld vir die heiliges van God om na te boots nie. Die gekabbelde geluid wat ons uit baie verbyryende voertuie hoor, weerspieël beslis die liedere van sulke vroulike voëls. “Babylon the great is fallen, is fallen, and is become the habitation of devils, and the hold of every foul spirit, and a cage of every unclean and hateful bird” (Rev 18:2). Hierdie oorvloedige wesens is die gevalle geeste, die voëls wat wag om die saad wat by die pad gesaai is te verslind. Van so is die waardelose swartvoëls, sterrevoëls en grackles. Die kraaie vertoon hulle ook langs die pad en voed op rotte karkasse. Dikwels sal jy hulle in groot getalle vind wat hulself voed aan die koring wat die boer noukeurig vir homself geplant het. So oortree die selfsugtige siel in sy strewe na geluk, voed vrolik op die rampspoed van 'n ander en exploit hulle sonde. Hy dra geen lied nie, want sy dag is voortdurend bewolk deur die boosheid van ander wat sy pad kruis.

Verwaarlosing. Die koevoël is ook swart (die wyfie is bruin/grys). Sy sal op 'n hoë uitkyk gesien word en skaamteloos haar liefdes roep met 'n skril gekras. Sy het dan die durf om haar eier in 'n ander voël se nes te lê en hulle te dwing om haar nageslag groot te maak. Dit is beslis 'n geskikte emblem vir 'n goeie aantal vroue in ons tyd. Al word dit deur omstandighede geregverdig, gee hierdie vroue nie om vir hul eie nie, maar is produkte van verwaarlosing. Hulle het geen slaaplied om met hul kleintjies te deel nie, want hulle het hulle na 'n ander se nes vergesel terwyl haar gedagtes met werk en besigheid besig is. “But thou art he that took me out of the womb: thou didst make me hope when I was upon my mother’s breasts” (Ps 22:9). Geen twyfel dat die singende moeder menigte liedere in haar baba kan inplant en die verhoog vir 'n gelukkige en hoopvolle lewe kan stel nie. Al mag ons barmhartigheid aan 'n vrou in moeilike omstandighede betoon, dra die moderne vrou se hooflied tog snare wat net dissonant en treurig is. Dit is toegepropte fonteine soos die putte wat Isak gevind het toe hy na Gerar teruggekeer het. Die Filistyne “had filled them with earth” (Gen 26:15). So loop die geestelik verwaarloosde huise van baie gesinne vandag, wat hul skedules so vol van aardse verpligtinge pak dat hulle nie tyd het om 'n uur saam in lied te bestee nie. As die voëls ophou sing, sou hulle dit eers opmerk?

Onverbeterlikheid. Vind 'n siel wat in ondankbaarheid gedoop is, en jy sal 'n siel sonder 'n lied vind. As die kanarie in gevangenskap geweier het om te sing, sou min van ons ooit sy vrolike melodie gehoor het. “We hanged our harps upon the willows in the midst thereof. For there they that carried us away captive required of us a song; and they that wasted us required of us mirth, saying, Sing us one of the songs of Zion. How shall we sing the LORD’S song in a strange land?” (Ps 137:2-4). God se volk was deur Jeremia aangesê om huise te bou, tuine te plant en gesinne groot te maak. “… And seek the peace of the city whither I have caused you to be carried away captives, and pray unto the LORD for it: for in the peace thereof shall ye have peace” (Jer. 29:5-7). Maar hulle kon geen waarde daarin sien nie. Met hul oë op die sombere toneel rondom hulle gefokus, het hulle hul lied verloor. Israel het binne sy geskiedenis 'n ryk tradisie van lied gehad. Hul gesang het by die deurgang van die Rooi See gebars in die dae van Jehoshaphat en was bekend daarvoor om leërs te ontset. Aardse ongemak is geen verskoning om dankbaarheid te ontken nie, want ons God regeer, en ons is Sy kinders. Só was die toestande in die Filipiër-gevangenis waar twee tronkvoëls, Paulus en Silas, die middernagkonsert geopen het en die gange met hul vreugdevolle gesang laat dreun het.

Wanneer ons ons monde oopmaak en ons vokale strek in lof, beeld ons die genade van God uit. Ons voeg by die getroue koor langs Miriam, Deborah en Hannah en meng harmonies met Moses, David, Paul en Barnabas. Saans sing ons saam met ons Here en Sy dissipels ná die ete, en met legioene engele “giving glory to God in the highest.” As dit nie genoeg is nie, moet ons miskien oorweeg om vroegoggend op te staan en saam te sing met die ontelbare skares van ons gevlerkte vriende wat dankbaar is vir God se liefdevolle voorzienigheid. “Let the word of Christ dwell in you richly in all wisdom; teaching and admonishing one another in psalms and hymns and spiritual songs, singing with grace in your hearts to the Lord … And whatsoever ye do, do it heartily, as to the Lord, and not unto men” (Col 3:16, 23).

The urgency of the last minute is something that many homemakers deal with regularly. No matter how organized we are, sometimes we put off tasks because we dislike them or wait until we are under pressure.

Habitual procrastination potentially leads to higher levels of stress. Maybe I’m odd, but it is hard for me to stay calm and collected when the pressure is mounting. By the time the last minute things are completed I’m too exhausted to enjoy the planned event.

Toothaches and Road Trips

It is a mystery to me why a family member ends up in a dentist chair a day or two before we leave on a trip. Maybe it hasn’t happened as often as I think, but the frustration of an unplanned trip to the dentist at an inopportune time is riveted in my mind. Now I schedule an imaginary appointment before a trip. If it is not a dental emergency, some other issue is bound to fill that time slot.

Deadlines are a normal part of life. Without them we would be unmotivated, and our days would lack purpose. Interruptions are also a normal part of life. They constantly give an unpredictable twist to our days and weeks. If we let too many tasks wait until the last minute, interruptions and deadlines collide, and chaos reigns.

Change the Last-Minute Scenario

Deadlines and interruptions cannot be eliminated but we can limit last-minute tasks. Sometimes it takes some honest looking back to figure out what caused our stress. Often, we blame it on interruptions and fail to realize that poor planning or procrastination might have been the culprit.

For example, if guests are coming and we plan to wash windows and make a dessert along with a dozen more tasks on the day of their arrival, there is no room for disruptions. From experience, we know interruptions will come. So, isn’t it better to “plan” for a bee sting and a stubbed toe?

Why not schedule window washing and dessert another day? That might mean some fingerprints on the windows and a simpler dessert, but isn’t that better than a great deal of stress at the last minute?

Do some tasks ahead of time

Deciding early in the day what to make for supper and packing the diaper bag in advance are little things that can make a big difference at the last minute. When our children were young, I started packing suitcases a day before a trip versus the day of leaving. I was better able to cope with the last-minute rush if that job was out of the way.

Do the most important tasks first

This approach gives freedom to skip jobs of lesser importance when up against a time crunch.

Sometimes not everything on the task list is of equal value. Dropping a task is difficult for a perfectionist, but it is possible to develop new habits.

Break work into smaller bits

Sometimes the enormity of a task makes it seem too huge to start. Break down the large task into smaller components. Completing a smaller task is much more manageable. Deep cleaning my kitchen is a task that I do not enjoy. If my planner says, “deep-clean kitchen,” it’s easy to ignore.

But if my planner says, “clean appliances, wipe out cupboards, and wash windows,” it seems more doable.

There are so many joyful events in life; why be hassled by procrastination? Give yourself the liberty to live life differently. A few minor changes can make the biggest difference between a blessed or stressed last minute.

Die dringency van die laaste minuut is iets waarmee baie tuistes gereeld te doen het. Maak nie saak hoe georganiseerd ons is nie, soms stel ons take uit omdat ons dit nie graag doen nie of wag tot ons onder druk is.

Gereelde uitstel kan moontlik lei tot hoër vlakke van spanning. Miskien is ek vreemd, maar dit is moeilik vir my om kalm en byderhand te bly wanneer die druk toeneem. Teen die tyd dat die laaste-minuut-dinge gedoen is, is ek te uitgeput om van die beplande gebeurtenis te geniet.

Tandpyn en Paduitstappies

Dit is ’n raaisel vir my waarom ’n familielid gewoonlik in ’n tandartsstoel beland een of twee dae voordat ons op ’n reis vertrek. Miskien het dit nie so gereeld gebeur as wat ek dink nie, maar die frustrasie van ’n onbeplande tandartsbesoek op ’n ongeleentheidstyd is vasgespes in my gedagtes. Nou beplan ek ’n denkbeeldige afspraak vóór ’n reis. As dit nie ’n tandheelkundige noodgeval is nie, sal ’n ander probleem seker daardie tydgleuf vul.

Sperdatums is ’n normale deel van die lewe. Sonder hulle sou ons ongemotiveerd wees, en ons dae sou doel ontbreek. Onderbrekings is ook ’n normale deel van die lewe. Hulle gee voortdurend ’n onvoorspelbare wending aan ons dae en weke. As ons te veel take tot die laaste minuut laat wag, bots onderbrekings en sperdatums, en heers chaos.

Verander die laaste-minuut-scenario

Sperdatums en onderbrekings kan nie uitgepluis word nie, maar ons kan laaste-minuut-take beperk. Soms verg dit ’n eerlike terugkyk om uit te vind wat ons spanning veroorsaak het. Dikwels gee ons die skuld aan onderbrekings en besef nie dat swak beplanning of uitstel die oorsaak kon wees nie.

Byvoorbeeld, as gaste kom en ons beplan om vensters te was en ’n nagereg te maak saam met ’n dosyn ander take op die dag van hul aankoms, is daar geen ruimte vir ontwrigtinge nie. Uit ervaring weet ons onderbrekings sal kom. Is dit dus nie beter om vir ’n bye-steek en ’n verstapte toon te “beplan” nie?

Hoekom nie vensterwas en nagereg op ’n ander dag skeduleer nie? Dit mag beteken daar is ’n paar vingerafdrukke op die vensters en ’n eenvoudiger nagereg, maar is dit nie beter as baie spanning op die laaste minuut nie?

Doen sommige take vooruit

Vroeg in die dag besluit wat om vir aandete te maak en die doopsak vooraf in te pak is klein dinge wat ’n groot verskil by die laaste minuut kan maak. Toe ons kinders nog jonk was, het ek begin om tasse ’n dag vóór ’n reis te pak in plaas van op die dag van vertrek. Ek kon beter met die laaste-minuut-haas klaarkom as daardie taak uit die pad was.

Doen die belangrikste take eerste

Hierdie benadering gee vryheid om take van minder belang oor te slaan wanneer daar tydsdruk is.

Partykeer is nie alles op die takelys van gelyke waarde nie. Om ’n taak te laat vaar is moeilik vir ’n perfeksionis, maar dit is moontlik om nuwe gewoontes te ontwikkel.

Breek werk in kleiner stukkies

Partykeer maak die enormiteit van ’n taak dit te groot om te begin. Breek die groot taak in kleiner komponente. Om ’n kleiner taak te voltooi is veel meer hanteerbaar. Om my kombuis diep skoon te maak is ’n taak wat ek nie geniet nie. As my beplanner sê, “diep skoon kombuis,” is dit maklik om te ignoreer.

Maar as my beplanner sê, “maak toestelle skoon, vee kaste uit en was vensters,” lyk dit meer doenbaar.

Daar is soveel vreugdevolle gebeurtenisse in die lewe; waarom laat uitstel jou terg? Gee jouself die vryheid om anders te lewe. ’n Paar minder veranderinge kan die grootste verskil maak tussen ’n geseënde of gespanne laaste minuut.

“Dr. Waldron, Elsie needs help!” Elsie’s husband was adamant, almost angry, as he stared at me. On the other hand, Elsie stared at the floor, almost as though she wasn’t present. I had never met either of the couple before and was struggling just a little to figure out what was needed from me to help her.

“What is going on?” I asked as I flipped through her chart. This was still in the days of paper charts, and I headed to the lab section of her chart. There wasn’t anything too crazy that I could see there—her liver enzymes were a little elevated, but otherwise, everything seemed OK.

“It’s her drinking!” Her husband told me. “She is drinking more and more every night. She won’t go out except to get whiskey. She drinks till she passes out every night and has to have something every morning to get her started.”

“Is that true?” I asked Elsie, feeling like a judge overseeing a jury trial.

“Yes,” she said. Her face was emotionless, and I couldn’t tell if she wanted to be there or not.

“Do you want help?” I asked her. This was a loaded question. Many people who struggle with alcoholism aren’t ready to break free from its vice-like hold on them. Maybe Elsie was different.

“I guess so,” she said, indifferently. Once again, I couldn’t tell whether she wanted to be there or not.

“At the rate at which you are drinking, you will kill yourself within a year – maybe two at best – if you don’t give up alcohol entirely,” I told her. “If you want to, I will try to find you an inpatient program to detox you and get you off of alcohol.”

“She’s ready,” he husband said firmly.

When dealing with someone who drinks heavily, it is crucial that they don’t simply stop drinking without medical support. Abrupt cessation of alcohol use causes the body to go into withdrawal which can produce a state called Delirium Tremens and even seizures.

I stepped out of the exam room and to make phone calls. It is never easy to find a place for someone to attempt to rehabilitate from any kind of substances, and it was over an hour and a half before I found a facility that was willing to take Elsie and try to help her get off of the whiskey.

I sighed as I reentered her exam room. I had been afraid that I wouldn’t find anywhere for her to go.

I told them about the plan, and her husband nodded vigorously, while Elise continued to stare silently at the floor. “Can we pray together before you go?” I asked them, and when they nodded assent, I prayed with them, asking for freedom and Jesus’ presence in both of their lives.

They left my office with marching orders and directions on where to go. I had a happy glow about me for the rest of the morning, knowing that I had gone the extra mile and had really made a difference in this middle-aged couple’s life.

Around 2 pm, I got a call from the rehab facility. They hadn’t seen even a shadow of Elsie or her husband, which was surprising, since it was a bright sunny day and the facility wasn’t that far away. With a sinking feeling, I dialed the couple’s phone number.

“She won’t go!” Her husband told me. “She tells me that she told me this ahead of time. She’ll try to cut back, but she isn’t willing to go into a rehab facility or any such thing. I guess just tell them that we’ll let them know if she changes her mind.”

My nurse called the rehab facility and told them the bad news, and I sat down in my chair, stunned. What else could I have done? Was there a solution for Elsie—something different that I could have said that would have made a difference in her life?

About a year later, I received the sad news that Elsie had died at home. I was certain that things would have been different if she had gone to rehab and if she had given control to Jesus. None of that had happened, and I felt cynicism pushing into my heart.

Cynicism

We live in an age of cynicism. In ancient Greece, the cynics were an odd assortment of men who specialized in being grouchy and saying mean (they would have said truthful) things to people. They often dressed in rags and behaved in such a way that most of the polite Athenians did not want to be close to them.

Today, cynicism means a tendency to believe the worst about people and circumstances. Cynical people believe that all people are motivated purely by selfishness and that bad events will tend to prevail.

Many young doctors are idealistic and very hopeful. They believe that if they exert the utmost effort, they can make a real, positive impact on their patient’s lives. Unfortunately, as time goes by and they try their hardest and their patients don’t change, they can give up. These doctors still try, but they no longer really hope that their efforts will make much of a difference.

It seems as though people who get involved with politics often have the best of intentions. They see this as a path to changing society for the better. Unfortunately, as time goes by and the faces in charge change, the policies don’t really change, they tend to become cynical.

Sometimes this cynicism is directed against all politicians. Sometimes it is only anger directed against members of the party that opposes their party’s positions. Hope is replaced by cynicism.

Cynicism in the Bible

If there is a book in the Bible that seems to have been written by a cynical man, it is the book of Ecclesiastes. The Preacher, who we understand to be Solomon, lists all of the things that he endeavored in an attempt to find joy.

In chapter 2:17-23 Solomon describes work as futile. He finishes by saying, “For what hath man of all his labour, and of the vexation of his heart, wherein he hath laboured under the sun? For all his days are sorrows, and his travail grief; yea, his heart taketh not rest in the night. This is also vanity.” (Ecclesiastes 2:22,23)

He saw the world as being dominated by tyrants and there was little that the people could do about it. Solomon went so far as to say that political power was meaningless “Better is a poor and a wise child than an old and foolish king, who will no more be admonished. For out of prison he cometh to reign; whereas also he that is born in his kingdom becometh poor” (Ecclesiastes 4:13).

In Ecclesiastes 6:6, he seems to disparage long life. “Yea, though he live a thousand years twice told, yet hath he seen no good: do not all go to one place?”

Of course, he finishes his short book with the instruction to remember our Creator in the days of our youth. There is a blessing for those who choose to focus on God when they have a little bit of energy left and not, when they are old and jaded, like Solomon.

Later on, it almost seemed as though God had given up on His people. He still sent prophets to them, but He knew without a doubt that the people would refuse to respond. “Therefore thou shalt speak all these words unto them; but they will not hearken to thee: thou shalt also call unto them; but they will not answer thee” (Jeremiah 7:27).

Even in the New Testament, Paul told Timothy that the time was coming when people would no longer listen to sound doctrine. “For the time will come when they will not endure sound doctrine; but after their own lusts shall they heap to themselves teachers, having itching ears;” (2 Timothy 4:3).

By picking and choosing these passages, we can come away with a very gloomy view of the future and, more specifically, of human’s willingness to change. It seems there is little point of investing ourselves in the people around us. They are full of woe and are as likely to change as a chipmunk is to master differential calculus.

The Opposite of Cynicism

The opposite of cynicism is hope. It is the belief that the future could be better.

It is interesting that the Apostle Paul spoke of tribulations in the Epistle to the Romans, “And not only so, but we glory in tribulations also: knowing that tribulation worketh patience; and patience, experience; and experience, hope: and hope maketh not ashamed; because the love of God is shed abroad in our hearts by the Holy Ghost which is given unto us” (Romans 5:3-5).

We may not have reached the place where we glory in the trials we experience, but certainly, they should bring us these other things that he mentions. For, we grow in patience and experience, even as we deal with trials, but more than that, we come to realize that we have hope for tomorrow because we serve a great God.

The contrast in the story of the Prodigal Son in Luke 15 teaches us much about hope. The father and the older brother were strikingly different in their attitudes.

The father had never given up hope – he knew that his son had failed him and gone far from what he knew was right and yet, the father still desired to see the prodigal come to himself and return home.

On the other hand, the older brother not only had no hope for his younger brother, but he was also angry with him. The prodigal had wasted his money, he had lived in sin, and now, he had returned home just because he was out of money.

Certainly, there was no reason to trust the younger son. Yet, that is exactly what our Heavenly Father does for us.

Look for Hope in the Right Places

Part of the problem is that we look for hope in the wrong places. A number of years ago, a presidential candidate ran for office under the slogan “Hope and Change,” and yet, even though he was elected, I imagine most folks did not feel that their lives were significantly changed for the better.

Pursuing the things this world values—political power and wealth is guaranteed to bring emptiness. This is Satan’s pattern—he always over-promises and under-delivers.

This was what he did when he tempted Jesus, “All these things will I give thee, if thou wilt fall down and worship me” (Matthew 4:8). All of the things Satan offered, nothing compared with the glory that Jesus eventually received from the road that led to the cross.

In the same way, Satan would like to distract Christians from seeking the things that are valuable, and that will bring hope. Satan tells Christians that politics will not only change the world for the better, it is an easier way to change the world.

The Bible is clear that we build hope as we nurture our relationship with God and then work to help our brothers and sisters build that same relationship in their own lives. The reason that we can hope is not because people are so wonderful—we don’t have to live very long to realize that they aren’t. The reason we hope is because we serve an awesome, faithful God who walks with us through the worst of our trials.

Remember that We Have Undeserved Hope

Jesus’ messages about forgiveness make it clear that one of the major reasons that we have for forgiving others in our lives is that we have received great and undeserved forgiveness. The same is true for hope.

Each one of us was hopeless and without reason to expect to receive hope and we were still given a ray of light in the midst of our darkness. Maybe part of the reason that we have so much trouble hoping for good things for the people around us is that we do not remember how hopeless we were before we found grace.

If Jesus was able to bring hope to our hopeless existence, then certainly He can do wonderful things in the hearts and lives of others around us. The only people we should give up on are the ones that our Savior has given up on as well.

Small Efforts Do Make a Difference

I remember having a conversation with a young person who was planning to go into medicine and had a plan to go to a foreign country and serve the people there. As we were talking, an older man entered the conversation and shared that he saw little hope for change in developing countries.

The people in those countries just weren’t interested in getting better and didn’t do the minimum necessary to stave off things like worms and parasites. Doctors and nurses couldn’t make a difference in such an environment.

I could sense the heart of the youth sinking as this older man shared. He had experience, and he had given up hope. The sad thing was that he was also stealing the hope of someone who still had a desire to serve.

When I was in training, I had a surgeon tell me that family doctors didn’t really do anything. They simply kept their patients alive till their next office visit, whereas surgeons really “fixed” people—taking out (or off) the offending body part.

At the end of the day, small efforts do make a difference. I don’t do brain surgery, but I still can make a difference in someone else’s life— maybe just by spending a little time and listening and praying. This is true for all of us.

More than that, we come to realize that making this effort changes our own lives for the better. Jesus told the sheep that as they ministered to “the least of these my brethren,” they were ministering to Him.

Even if no one’s life is improved, our Savior knows our desires and feels our efforts, and will reward them someday.

A Few Things to Remember

When we face failures, we tend to move in one of two directions. Those of us who are optimists tend to believe that this episode was an isolated event and that the future is still bright. On the other hand, pessimists believe that failures are permanent, personal, and pervasive.

Pessimists believe that their failures are the result of intrinsic character flaws that they have and that these things affect all of their lives and are unlikely to change. Unlike the righteous man who falls to rise again, these people fall and lie where they fall, defeated at the outset.

When we are dealing with other people, we need to give them the same grace that we should give ourselves. They, too, are growing, and if they have a failure today, they will do better tomorrow. Maybe they will fail again, but they will at least “fail better.”

Conclusion

Cynicism is rife in our world. Many have given up hope for a better future, and it is understandable for those who have invested their hope in this world’s institutions. There is no real hope in government or in armies or in bureaucracy.

The song says, “Oh to have no hope in Jesus, how dark this world must be!” For, Jesus is the one who brings light into our darkness and allows us to continue, even when others fail us.

God is the one who redeems us. He is the one who sent the prophets, even though their messages were ignored, and the prophets were persecuted. He is the one who continues to hope for us, even when we have failed Him so many times in the past.

He is the reason we carry on. He is the reason that we have hope, not only for ourselves but also for our brothers.

“Dr. Waldron, Elsie het hulp nodig!” Elsie se man was vasberade, byna kwaad, terwyl hy na my staar. Aan die ander kant het Elsie na die vloer gestaar, amper asof sy nie teenwoordig was nie. Ek het nog nooit van die paartjie tevore ontmoet nie en het effens gesukkel om vas te stel wat van my nodig was om haar te help.

“Wat gebeur hier?” het ek gevra terwyl ek deur haar dossier blaai. Dit was nog in die dae van papierdossiers, en ek het na die laboratoriumafdeling van haar dossier gegaan. Daar was niks baie vreemd wat ek daar gesien het nie—haar lewerensieme was effens verhoog, maar anders het alles goed gelyk.

“Dit is haar drink!” het haar man vir my gesê. “Sy drink elke aand meer en meer. Sy gaan nie uit nie behalwe om whiskey te koop. Sy drink totdat sy flou val elke aand en moet iets hê elke oggend om haar aan die gang te kry.”

“Is dit waar?” het ek vir Elsie gevra, en gevoel asof ek ’n regter is wat ’n jurie oorsee hou.

“Ja,” het sy gesê. Haar gesig was emosieloos, en ek kon nie sê of sy daar wou wees of nie.

“Wil jy hulp hê?” het ek haar gevra. Dit was ’n gelaaide vraag. Baie mense wat sukkel met alkoholisme is nie gereed om vry te breek van die stywe greep wat dit op hulne het nie. Miskien was Elsie anders.

“Ek dink so,” het sy sê, ongeïndifiseer. Weer kon ek nie sê of sy daar wou wees of nie.

“Teen die tempo waarop jy drink, sal jy jouself binne ’n jaar – miskien twee op die beste – doodmaak as jy nie heeltemal met alkohol ophou nie,” het ek vir haar gesê. “As jy wil, sal ek probeer om ’n inrigting te vind wat jou indrinkingsentoksikeer en jou van alkohol af kry.”

“Sy is gereed,” het die man ferm gesê.

Wanneer jy te doen het met iemand wat swaar drink, is dit noodsaaklik dat hulle nie net ophou drink sonder mediese ondersteuning nie. Skielike staking van alkoholgebruik veroorsaak dat die liggaam onttrekking ondergaan wat ’n toestand kan oplewer wat Delirium Tremens genoem word en selfs stuiptrekkings kan veroorsaak.

Ek het die ondersoekkamer verlaat om telefone te maak. Dit is nooit maklik om ’n plek te vind vir iemand om rehabilitasie vir enige soort middels te probeer nie, en dit het meer as ’n uur en ’n half geneem voordat ek ’n fasiliteit gevind het wat bereid was om Elsie te neem en te probeer help om van die whiskey af te kom.

Ek het ’n sug geslaak toe ek weer my ondersoekkamer ingegaan het. Ek was bang dat ek nêrens sou vind vir haar om heen te gaan nie.

Ek het hulle van die plan vertel, en haar man het kragtig geknik, terwyl Elsie voortgegaan het om swaar na die vloer te staar. “Kan ons saam bid voordat jy gaan?” het ek vir hulle gevra, en toe hulle instem, het ek saam met hulle gebid en gevra vir vryheid en Jesus se teenwoordigheid in beide van hulle lewens.

Hulle het my kantoor verlaat met marsbevelle en aanwysings waarheen om te gaan. Ek het die res van die oggend ’n warm gevoel gehad, wetende dat ek die ekstra myl geloop het en regtig ’n verskil in hierdie middeljarige paartjie se lewe gemaak het.

Omstreeks 14:00 het ek ’n oproep van die rehabilitasiefasiliteit ontvang. Hulle het nie eens ’n skaduwee van Elsie of haar man gesien nie, wat verrassend was, aangesien dit ’n helder sonnige dag was en die fasiliteit nie so ver weg was nie. Met ’n sinking gevoel het ek die paartjie se nommer gedraai.

“Sy wil nie gaan nie!” het haar man vir my gesê. “Sy sê sy het my dit vantevore gesê. Sy sal probeer om minder te drink, maar sy is nie bereid om in ’n ontwenningsinrigting of iets dergeliks te gaan nie. Ek raai net sê vir hulle dat ons hulle sal laat weet as sy van plan verander.”

My suster het die rehabilitasiefasiliteit gebel en hulle die slegte nuus meegedeel, en ek het in my stoel gaan sit, stomgeslaan. Wat anders kon ek gedoen het? Was daar ’n oplossing vir Elsie—iets anders wat ek kon gesê het wat ’n verskil in haar lewe sou gemaak het?

Ongeveer ’n jaar later het ek die hartseer nuus ontvang dat Elsie by die huis dood is. Ek was seker dat dinge anders sou gewees het as sy na rehabilitasie gegaan het en as sy beheer aan Jesus oorgegee het. Niks van dit het gebeur nie, en ek het gevoel hoe sinisme in my hart begin inkries.

Cynisme

Ons leef in ’n era van sinisme. In antieke Griekeland was die cynici ’n eienaardige mengsel van mans wat daarop gespesialiseer het om knorrig te wees en na die mense onvriendelike (hulle sou gesê het waarheidsgetroue) dinge te sê. Hulle het dikwels in lompe gedra en so behandel dat die meeste van die beleefde Atheners nie naby hulle wou wees nie.

Vandag beteken sinisme ’n neiging om die ergste van mense en omstandighede te glo. Cyniese mense glo dat alle mense suiwer deur selfbelang gemotiveer word en dat slegte gebeure geneig is om te oorheers.

Baie jong dokters is idealisties en baie hoopvol. Hulle glo dat as hulle uiterste moeite doen, hulle ’n werklike, positiewe impak op hul pasiënte se lewens kan maak. Ongelukkig, soos tyd verbygaan en hulle hul bes doen en hul pasiënte nie verander nie, kan hulle opgee. Hierdie dokters probeer nog steeds, maar hulle hoop nie regtig dat hul pogings veel van ’n verskil sal maak nie.

Dit lyk asof mense wat betrokke raak by politiek dikwels die beste bedoelings het. Hulle sien dit as ’n pad om die samelewing vir die beter te verander. Ongelukkig, soos tyd verbygaan en die gesigte aan die bewind verander, verander die beleide nie regtig nie, en hulle neig om sinies te raak.

Soms is hierdie sinisme gerig teen alle politici. Soms is dit net woede gerig teen lede van die party wat die teenparty se standpunte teenstaan. Hoop word vervang deur sinisme.

Cynisme in die Bybel

As daar ’n boek in die Bybel is wat lyk of dit deur ’n sinsgetrewe man geskryf is, is dit die boek Prediker. Die Prediker, wat ons verstaan as Salomo, tel al die dinge op waaraan hy hom gegee het in ’n poging om vreugde te vind.

In hoofstuk 2:17-23 beskryf Salomo werk as sinloos. Hy eindig deur te sê, “For what hath man of all his labour, and of the vexation of his heart, wherein he hath laboured under the sun? For all his days are sorrows, and his travail grief; yea, his heart taketh not rest in the night. This is also vanity.” (Ecclesiastes 2:22,23)

Hy het die wêreld as oorheers deur tiranne gesien en daar was min wat die mense daaraan kon doen. Salomo het selfs so ver gegaan om te sê dat politieke mag betekenisloos was: “Better is a poor and a wise child than an old and foolish king, who will no more be admonished. For out of prison he cometh to reign; whereas also he that is born in his kingdom becometh poor” (Ecclesiastes 4:13).

In Prediker 6:6 lyk dit asof hy lang lewe kleinpraat. “Yea, though he live a thousand years twice told, yet hath he seen no good: do not all go to one place?”

Natuurlik eindig hy sy kort boek met die opdrag om ons Skepper te onthou in die dae van ons jeug. Daar is ’n seën vir diegene wat kies om op God te fokus wanneer hulle nog ’n bietjie krag oor het en nie, wanneer hulle oud en versadig is nie, soos Salomo.

Later het dit byna gelyk asof God opgegee het met Sy volk. Hy het steeds profete na hulle gestuur, maar Hy het sonder twyfel geweet dat die mense sou weier om te reageer. “Therefore thou shalt speak all these words unto them; but they will not hearken to thee: thou shalt also call unto them; but they will not answer thee” (Jeremiah 7:27).

Selfs in die Nuwe Testament het Paulus aan Timoteus gesê dat die tyd sou kom wanneer mense nie meer na gesonde leer sou luister nie. “For the time will come when they will not endure sound doctrine; but after their own lusts shall they heap to themselves teachers, having itching ears;” (2 Timothy 4:3).

Deur hierdie gedeeltes selektief te kies, kan ons met ’n baie droë siening van die toekoms en, meer spesifiek, van die mens se bereidheid tot verandering uitkom. Dit lyk asof daar min sin is om onsself in die mense rondom ons te belê. Hulle is vol ellende en is net so geneig om te verander as ’n grondeekhoorn om differensiaalrekening te bemeester.

Die Teenoorgestelde van Cynisme

Die teenoorgestelde van sinisme is hoop. Dit is die geloof dat die toekoms beter kan wees.

Dit is interessant dat die apostel Paulus oor verdrukkinge gespreek het in die Briedbrief aan die Romeine, “And not only so, but we glory in tribulations also: knowing that tribulation worketh patience; and patience, experience; and experience, hope: and hope maketh not ashamed; because the love of God is shed abroad in our hearts by the Holy Ghost which is given unto us” (Romans 5:3-5).

Ons mag dalk nie al die manier bereik het waar ons ryk is in die verheerliking van die beproewinge wat ons ervaar nie, maar sekerlik behoort hulle ons die ander dinge wat hy noem te bring. Want ons groei in geduld en ervaring, selfs terwyl ons met beproewinge te doen het, maar meer as dit, ons kom agter dat ons hoop vir môre het omdat ons ’n groot God dien.

Die kontras in die verhaal van die Verloren Seun in Lukas 15 leer ons baie oor hoop. Die vader en die ouer broer was opvallend anders in hul houdings.

Die vader het nooit die hoop opgegee nie—hy het geweet dat sy seun hom teleurgestel het en ver van regte gedrag afgewyk het en tog het die vader steeds begeer om die verlorene by homself te sien kom en huis toe te kom.

Aan die ander kant het die ouer broer nie net geen hoop vir sy jonger broer gehad nie, maar hy was ook kwaad vir hom. Die verlorene het sy geld vermors, hy het in sonde geleef, en nou het hy net huis toe gekom omdat hy geen geld meer gehad het nie.

Beslis was daar geen rede om die jonger seun te vertrou nie. Tog is dit presies wat ons Hemelse Vader vir ons doen.

Kyk na Hoop op die Regte Plekke

’n Deel van die probleem is dat ons hoop in die verkeerde plekke soek. ’n Aantal jare gelede het ’n presidensiële kandidaat onder die slogaan “Hope and Change” aangetree, en tog, alhoewel hy verkies is, dink ek nie die meeste mense het gevoel dat hul lewens beduidend vir die beter verander het nie.

Om die dinge na te jaag wat hierdie wêreld waardeer—politiese mag en rykdom—is gedoem om leegheid te bring. Dit is Satan se patroon—hy belê voortdurend te veel en lewer te min.

Dit was wat hy gedoen het toe hy Jesus versoek het, “All these things will I give thee, if thou wilt fall down and worship me” (Matthew 4:8). Al die dinge wat Satan aangebied het, vergelyk met niks met die heerlikheid wat Jesus uiteindelik ontvang het deur die pad wat na die kruis gelei het nie.

Op dieselfde manier sou Satan graag Christene wil aflei van die soeke na die dinge wat waardevol is en wat hoop sal bring. Satan sê vir Christene dat politiek nie net die wêreld vir die beter sal verander nie, dit is ’n makliker manier om die wêreld te verander.

Die Bybel is duidelik dat ons hoop bou soos ons ons verhouding met God koester en dan werk om ons boeties en susters te help om dieselfde verhouding in hul eie lewens te bou. Die rede dat ons kan hoop is nie omdat mense so wonderlik is nie—ons hoef nie lank te lewe om te besef dat hulle nie is nie. Die rede waarom ons hoop, is omdat ons ’n ontsagwekkende, getroue God dien wat met ons loop deur die ergste van ons beproewinge.

Onthou dat ons Onverdiende Hoop Het

Jesus se boodskappe oor vergifnis maak dit duidelik dat een van die hoofredes wat ons het om ander te vergewe in ons lewens is dat ons groot en onverdiende vergifnis ontvang het. Dieselfde geld vir hoop.

Elkeen van ons was hooploos en sonder rede om te verwag om hoop te ontvang en tog is ons steeds gegee ’n straal lig te midde van ons duisternis. Miskien is deel van die rede dat ons so veel moeite het om vir goeie dinge te hoop vir die mense om ons heen dat ons nie onthou hoe hopeloos ons was voordat ons genade gevind het nie.

As Jesus in staat was om hoop in ons hopelose bestaan te bring, dan kan Hy beslis wonderlike dinge in die harte en lewens van ander rondom ons doen. Die enigste mense waarop ons moet opgee, is diegene wat ons Verlosser ook opgegee het.

Klein Pogings Maak Wel ’n Verskil

Ek onthou ’n gesprek met ’n jong persoon wat beplan het om medisyne te gaan studeer en ’n plan gehad het om na ’n vreemde land te gaan en die mense daar te dien. Terwyl ons gepraat het, het ’n ouer man by die gesprek aangesluit en gedeel dat hy min hoop gesien het vir verandering in ontwikkelende lande.

Die mense in daardie lande was net nie geïnteresseerd om beter te word nie en het nie die minimum gedoen wat nodig was om dinge soos wurms en parasiete af te weer nie. Dokters en verpleegsters kon nie ’n verskil maak in so ’n omgewing nie.

Ek kon die hart van die jongman voel sink toe hierdie ouer man dit deel. Hy het ervaring gehad, en hy het die hoop opgegee. Die hartseer ding was dat hy ook die hoop gesteel het van iemand wat nog ’n begeerte gehad het om te dien.

Toe ek in opleiding was, het ’n slagter my vertel dat huisdokters nie regtig iets doen nie. Hulle hou net hul pasiënte lewendig tot hul volgende kantoorbesoek, terwyl chirurge regtig mense “regmaak”—deur die aanstootlike liggaamsdeel te verwyder (of af te haal).

Aan die einde van die dag maak klein pogings wel ’n verskil. Ek doen nie breinkirurgie nie, maar ek kan steeds ’n verskil in iemand anders se lewe maak—miskien net deur ’n bietjie tyd spandeer en te luister en te bid. Dit is waar vir ons almal.

Meer as dit, ons kom agter dat om hierdie poging te doen ons eie lewens vir die beter verander. Jesus het aan die skape gesê dat toe hulle bedien het aan “the least of these my brethren,” hulle aan Hom bedien het.

Selfs as niemand se lewe verbeter nie, ken ons Verlosser ons begeertes en voel Hy ons pogings, en sal hulle eendag beloon.

’n Paar Dinge om te Onthou

Wanneer ons met mislukkings te doen kry, geneig ons om in een van twee rigtings te beweeg. Diegene van ons wat optimiste is, neig te glo dat hierdie episode ’n geïsoleerde gebeurtenis was en dat die toekoms steeds helder is. Aan die ander kant glo pessimis­te dat mislukkings permanent, persoonlik en alomteenwoordig is.

Pessimiste glo dat hul mislukkings die gevolg is van intrinsieke karakterfoute wat hulle het en dat hierdie dinge al hul lewens raak en waarskynlik nie sal verander nie. Anders as die regverdige man wat val om op te staan, val hierdie mense en lê waar hulle val, verslaan vanaf die begin.

Wanneer ons met ander mense te doen kry, moet ons hulle dieselfde genade gee wat ons onsself gee. Hulle groei ook, en as hulle vandag ’n mislukking het, sal hulle môre beter doen. Miskien sal hulle weer misluk, maar hulle sal ten minste “beter faal.”

Gevolgtrekking

Cynisme is wydverspreid in ons wêreld. Baie mense het die hoop op ’n beter toekoms opgegee, en dit is verstaanbaar vir diegene wat hul hoop in hierdie wêreld se instellings belê het. Daar is geen werklike hoop in regering of in leërmagte of in burokrasië nie.

Die lied sê, “Oh to have no hope in Jesus, how dark this world must be!” Want Jesus is die een wat lig in ons duisternis bring en ons in staat stel om aan te hou, selfs wanneer ander ons laat staan.

God is die een wat ons verlos. Hy is die een wat die profete gestuur het, al was hul boodskappe geïgnoreer en is die profete vervolg. Hy is die een wat steeds hoop vir ons het, selfs wanneer ons Hom soveel kere in die verlede verraai het.

Hy is die rede waarom ons aangaan. Hy is die rede dat ons hoop het, nie net vir onsself nie, maar ook vir ons broers.
